To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• the degree of a geometric algo- rthm can be formally defined and evaluated; • degree-driven algorithm design is an important paradigm; • the degree-driven paradigm is applicable to the problem of proximity queries; • the degree of proximity queries is optimal.

(i) the exact computation paradigm can be formalized in a way that is suitable for the design and evaluation of geometric algorithms; and (ii) in the context of proximity queries, our new approach is both fast and robust, and for the two-dimensional case, optimal with respect to all cost measures of the exact computation paradigm.

the exact-computation approach to robust geometric computing can be formalized as a paradigm with two cost measures, and that the degree of geometric algorithms can be evaluated expeditiously and used as a tool for algorithm design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of robust geometric computation and with the design of new algorithms for geometric problems.
the design, analysis and implementation of geometric algorithms with provably low degree, which is a new paradigm for the development of robust geometric algorithms.
the design of algorithms for geometric computations which are both ecient and robust.

we have presented a general methodology for the design of geometric algorithms that are both exact and robust, a formalism to expeditiously evaluate the cost of such algorithms in terms of both the number of arithmetic operations and the precision of arithmetic calculation, and a new and optimal technique for proximity queries.
we have presented a new paradigm for robust algorithmic design that is based on the degree of algorithms, and we have illustrated this paradigm by applying it to proximity queries.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that, in some cases, exact computation of geometric algorithms can be made ecient and that the degree paradigm is a powerful tool for this purpose.

we have introduced a new paradigm for the robust execution of geometric algorithms, and we have developed a new technique for proximity queries that illustrates the power and the promise of our paradigm.
we have introduced a paradigm that allows for the design of robust geometric algorithms with low degree.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by combining algorithm design and analysis with degree-driven algorithm design, we obtain a new technique for robust geometric algorithms with low degree, which in the case of proximity queries is optimal with regard to the cost measures of the exact computation paradigm.

the exact-computation methodology is an effective tool for the design of geometric algorithms that are robust with respect to the underlying computational model and, in particular, to the precision of arithmetic calculations.
the degree-driven approach is a powerful and general methodology for the development of robust geometric algorithms.
